body: The original issue here has already been fixed, can be checked on [updated repro](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-issue-repro2-8j6qcd?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts). (fixed version is 7.2.12)

@trotyl sorry for not getting back to you sooner. Unfortunately, the fix you mention is not satisfactory, as the fallback for `CSS.escape()` is not complete -- for instance, it doesn't deal with anchors that start with numbers.

I would recommend reverting the commit and using `getElementById` like in your PR. The `name` attribute selector works fine as long as the value is quoted and doesn't contain quotes `('|")`, which can be specifically escaped with a simple `replace` - e.g. 

```js
document.body.querySelector("[name='0\=[]#']"); // => null
```
I generally agree with you, but you'll still need to argue with Angular team on your own.

@axelboc - when I looked at the repro provided by @trotyl above (https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-issue-repro2-8j6qcd) I can see that there is an anchor starting with number and it works fine (at least on Chrome OS/X).  Can you clarify what is still missing?

Wow, this was a while ago, but looks like I was wrong: `CSS.escape` does handle IDs that start with numbers, you're right. The use case I mentioned works fine now, so feel free to close the issue.

---

For what it's worth, looking at the [implementation of `scrollToAnchor` on `master`](https://github.com/jasonaden/angular/blob/master/packages/common/src/viewport_scroller.ts#L112), which doesn't seem to have changed since #29577, I still find it silly to query the element with `this.document.querySelector(``#${anchor}``)`, when this could be done with `getElementById` without having to first escape the `anchor` (and risk forgetting to escape some characters...)

Why not attempt `getElementById` first, and only then, if it doesn't find anything, escape the `anchor` and try with `querySelector(``[name='${anchor}']``)`? This solution would even simplify the escaping regex (cf. my previous comment).
